title: How URL Filtering rule criteria combine

prose.text: Within one rule, criteria combine by a fixed expression. {{operator-expression}} Mostly AND, with three OR groups: identity (configurable OR or AND), location, and device.

prose.label: What ZIA can see.
prose.text: {{payload-criteria-need-inspection}} See [[zia.ssl-inspection.pipeline]] for when the full request is visible.

checks.do: Whether a criterion left empty is intended, since an unset criterion is ignored rather than matching nothing.
Whether a second URL Categories field is meant as an AND, which narrows the rule.
Whether a rule that matches on request method, protocol or path is applied to decrypted traffic.

operator-expression.statement: A rule matches when all four groups are true, joined by AND: Who, Where and When [ (Users OR/AND Groups OR/AND Departments) AND User Risk Profile AND Adaptive Access Profile AND (Location Groups OR Locations) AND Time ]; What [ Request Methods AND Protocols AND URL Categories AND User Agent AND HTTP Header Profiles ]; Source [ Source IP Groups AND Source Countries ]; and Device [ (Device Groups OR Devices) AND Workload Groups AND Device Trust Level ].
operator-expression.conditions: Corrected on recapture (2026-10-18): previously "A rule matches when this expression is true: Source IP Groups AND Source Countries AND URL Categories AND [Users OR/AND Groups OR/AND Departments] AND User Risk Profile AND [Location Groups OR Locations] AND Time AND Request Methods AND Protocols AND User Agent AND [Device Groups OR Devices] AND Device Trust.".

quotes: The logical relationship between the categories is AND, and the rule conditions within each category have their own set of logical operators applied, explained as follows:
Who, Where, & When: [ (Users OR/AND Groups OR/AND Departments) AND User Risk Profile AND Adaptive Access Profile AND (Location Groups OR Locations) AND Time ] AND
What: [ Request Methods AND Protocols AND URL Categories AND User Agent AND HTTP Header Profiles ] AND
Source: [ Source IP Groups AND Source Countries ] AND
Device: [ (Device Groups OR Devices) AND Workload Groups AND Device Trust Level ]

unset-ignored.statement: In URL Filtering rules, criteria such as URL Categories and Locations are ignored when left without a value, not treated as "matches nothing": leaving Locations empty removes location from the rule's evaluation.

evidence.after: URL Categories: Select any number of URL super categories or categories or both.
quotes: Selecting no value ignores this criterion in the policy evaluation.
Locations: Select up to 32 locations. Selecting no value ignores the criterion in the policy evaluation.

url-categories2-and.statement: A second URL Categories field (`urlCategories2` in the API) is ANDed with the first: the URL must be in a category from each field, which makes the rule narrower, not broader.

quotes: The URL Categories fields are connected with a logical AND operator.
The URL Categories fields are connected with a logical AND operator.
Note: The urlCategories and urlCategories2 parameters are connected with a logical AND operator

groups-and.statement: In the About URL Filtering rule table, the Groups fields are connected with a logical AND operator, as are the URL Categories fields.

quotes: The Groups fields are connected with a logical AND operator.
The URL Categories fields are connected with a logical AND operator.

rule-validity-period.statement: A rule can carry a Start Date and Time (the rule is valid starting this date and time), an End Date and Time (the rule ceases to be valid on this date and time) and a Time Zone in which the policy rule is valid.

quotes: Start Date and Time: The start date and time of the policy rule, if available. The rule is valid starting this date and time.
End Date and Time: The end date and time of the policy rule, if available. The rule ceases to be valid on this date and time.
Time Zone: The time zone in which the policy rule is valid.

https-user-policy.statement: The page says user-based URL policy on HTTPS traffic can be enforced in different ways, which it describes under SSL/TLS Inspection, IP surrogate and Kerberos. With SSL/TLS Inspection enabled, the service decrypts SSL/TLS transactions and sees the HTTP traffic in the tunnel (with the URI and the Zscaler cookie representing the user), and the location must have authentication enabled. If SSL/TLS interception is not feasible, the IP surrogate feature maps a user to a device IP address so the user's policies apply. With Kerberos, the service can enforce user, group and department policies on proxied HTTPS transactions without decrypting them; the location must have authentication and Kerberos enabled, and Kerberos authentication is supported only for traffic forwarded in explicit mode.

quotes: The Zscaler service can enforce user-based URL policies on HTTPS traffic in different ways.

When SSL/TLS Inspection is enabled, the Zscaler service decrypts SSL/TLS transactions and has full visibility of the HTTP traffic in the SSL/TLS tunnel (with URI and the Zscaler cookie representing the user), so it can enforce user policies.
The location must have authentication enabled.

If enabling SSL/TLS interception is not a feasible option for your organization, you can use the IP surrogate feature, which enables the Zscaler service to map a user to a device IP address so it can apply the user's policies.
The service can enforce granular user, group and department policies on proxied HTTPS transactions, without having to decrypt the HTTPS transactions.
The location must have authentication and Kerberos enabled.
The service supports Kerberos authentication only for traffic forwarded in explicit mode.

user-risk-score-levels.statement: The console's User Risk Profile criterion selects user risk score levels (by default Low 0–29, Medium 30–59, High 60–79, Critical 80–100). The API carries it as `userRiskScoreLevels`.
user-risk-score-levels.conditions: The console-label-to-field mapping is a chain of evidence: the help describes the criterion as risk score levels, and the rule model's only risk field is userRiskScoreLevels.

quotes: User Risk Profile: Select the user risk score levels to which the rule applies.
Low: Level with user risk scores ranging from 0 to 29
Critical: Level with user risk scores ranging from 80 to 100
UserRiskScoreLevels []string `json:"userRiskScoreLevels,omitempty"`

api-only-scoping.statement: The API also scopes rules by workload groups (`workloadGroups`) and by HTTP header profiles (`httpHeaderProfiles`).

quotes: // The list of preconfigured workload groups to which the policy must be applied.
// Name-ID pairs HTTP header profile to which the rule applies
WorkloadGroups []common.IDName `json:"workloadGroups,omitempty"`
HTTPHeaderProfiles []common.IDNameExtensions `json:"httpHeaderProfiles,omitempty"`

payload-criteria-need-inspection.statement: Criteria that need the request itself (Request Methods, Protocols, URL path) can only be evaluated on decrypted traffic; on uninspected HTTPS only domain-level evaluation exists, so such rules silently do not fire.
payload-criteria-need-inspection.conditions: Chain of evidence: pre-decrypt evaluation sees only the destination domain.

quotes: During a CONNECT request or an incoming SSL/TLS connection (SNI), only the destination domain is available and not the full URL.

two-category-fields-and.note: The URL is only in the first field's category, so the AND fails and the rule does not match.
